definitionBean.title: Combination Reaction
definitionBean.definition: A chemical reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product is called a combination reaction.
definitionBean.explanation: The key feature of this type of reaction is substances joining together to form a single product. It is often considered an exothermic reaction because energy is released.
importantPoints: Two or more reactants form a single product

definitionBean.title: Decomposition Reaction
definitionBean.definition: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give two or more simpler products is called a decomposition reaction.
definitionBean.explanation: This is completely opposite to a combination reaction. It requires heat, light, or electrical energy to break down reactants (endothermic).
importantPoints: Single reactant breaks into two or more products

questions.text: Quick Revision - Displacement and Double Displacement Reaction

definitionBean.title: Displacement and Double Displacement Reaction
definitionBean.definition: A reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound is called displacement; and exchange of ions is double displacement.
definitionBean.explanation: In displacement, one element takes the place of another, whereas in double displacement, ions are exchanged between two compounds to form new ones.
importantPoints: Displacement: Removal of a less reactive element by a more reactive one
Double Displacement: Exchange of ions between reactants
Precipitates are often formed in double displacement reactions

parts.statement: What is a combination reaction? Explain with an example.
parts.correct_answer: Two or more reactants combine to form a new product (e.g., combustion of coal).
parts.explanation: A chemical reaction in which two or more substances (reactants) combine to form only one new substance (product) is called a combination reaction. Example: Combustion of coal - $\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$.

parts.statement: Why is a decomposition reaction considered opposite to a combination reaction? Give an example.
parts.correct_answer: Decomposition breaks a reactant into multiple products, which is opposite to combination.
parts.explanation: In a combination reaction, two or more reactants form a product, whereas in a decomposition reaction, a single reactant breaks down into two or more products. Example: Electrolysis of water at the cathode.

parts.statement: What is a displacement reaction? Explain it using the experiment of an iron nail and copper sulfate solution.
parts.correct_answer: More reactive element displaces less reactive; iron displaces copper to form ferrous sulfate.
parts.explanation: When a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound solution, it is called a displacement reaction. When an iron nail is dipped in a blue copper sulfate solution, iron displaces copper to form ferrous sulfate and the solution turns green.

parts.statement: Can zinc displace copper from copper sulfate solution? Write the reason.
parts.correct_answer: Yes, because zinc is a more reactive metal than copper.
parts.explanation: Yes, zinc can displace copper from copper sulfate solution because zinc is a more reactive metal than copper.

parts.statement: What is meant by a double displacement reaction? Write a suitable equation.
parts.correct_answer: Exchange of ions between reactants is a double displacement reaction.
parts.explanation: Reactions in which there is an exchange of ions between reactants are called double displacement reactions. Example: $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)} + \text{BaCl}_2\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)} + \text{2NaCl(aq)}$.

parts.statement: What is called a precipitation reaction in double displacement reactions? Explain.
parts.correct_answer: A double displacement reaction that produces an insoluble solid (precipitate) is a precipitation reaction.
parts.explanation: Such a double displacement reaction in which an insoluble solid (precipitate) is formed is also called a precipitation reaction; e.g., formation of white precipitate of barium sulfate.
